effort: Read forward commitment, accelerate briefly and own the stop.
brief: Transfer Class 1’s body-read principle from side-to-side tracking to forward release. The main problem is initiating from real weight transfer without guessing. E1 is the live-release anchor; ankle rebound, forward impulse, staggered drive, a known brake and a forward ballistic release supply distinct physical jobs.
anchor_protocol: Coach and athlete face the same direction on parallel paths, coach half a step ahead. Coach visibly shifts weight and leaves after a variable 1–3 s interval; no verbal go. Athlete reads the departure, accelerates from 2 m to 5 m, and stops by 8 m. Six departures; reset by walking outside the active path. Record cue provider and start geometry. Hold a slower coach departure if initiation or stopping is not controlled.
quality_marker: For each of six E1 starts: movement after visible commitment, smooth first two steps, and stop before the 8 m line without a reaching locked-knee plant. Record correct read/control separately; no reaction-time claim.
layout: Use one 10 m athlete lane and a separate parallel coach path with at least 2 m verified separation. E1/E4 start at 2 m, travel 3 m, brake within 3 m, leaving 2 m at each end. Jump travel stays within 2–6 m, with a clear 2 m landing buffer. E6 releases a light medicine ball forward from 2 m into an empty 2–7 m catch-free landing zone; one thrower, retrieve only after the ball stops. Choose load/trajectory that remain inside it. If no ball is light enough for a fast low release, delivery of E6 requires an appropriate ball rather than extra loaded jumps.
progression: Previous: Class 1 prescribed lateral cue work, lateral lunge/split squat/RDL and adductor/calf loading; no actual work reported. Current: forward task, two-set goblet squat, one-set reverse lunge and retained hinge/ankle anchors. This changes force direction and reduces unilateral compound volume. Hold loads and the controlled-speed cue while feedback is absent. Advance later only when the actual full dose, 2–3 RIR, stopping control and recovery are documented; do not convert new drill success into a load increase.
audit: Kept the perceptual anchor first, limited forward and staggered jumps to three/four landings, and used one reverse-lunge set/leg to limit overlap with squat and RDL. Forward toss is a single low release, not a catch circuit. No Class 1 agility drill is repeated. Next class adds a no-go decision only if the coach can elicit a clear response to genuine commitment.

explosive.name: Forward Release Chase
explosive.job: Main live read-to-forward-drive task; identify opponent departure rather than memorizing a sound cue.
explosive.execution: Rapid first steps at a controllable speed; brake within 3 m. Rest 45 s between starts, 90 s between sets and 90 s before E2. Stop for guessing or boundary loss.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Forward–Back Line Hops
explosive.job: Quick fore–aft ankle return supports the first acceleration contacts and the later backward pressure of braking.
explosive.execution: Both feet cross a visible floor seam forward/back, four each way; low amplitude, stop after contact eight. Rest 60 s before E3; reduce amplitude for heel slap or ankle roll.
explosive.source: line-pogo-forward-back; exact bilateral direction verified locally

explosive.name: Standing Broad Jump to Stick
explosive.job: Whole-body forward impulse from a parallel stance, without a perceptual or unilateral landing demand.
explosive.execution: Two-foot takeoff and landing, natural arms; choose a controllable distance and hold 2 s. Rest 30 s between jumps, 60 s before E4. Shorten distance for extra steps.

explosive.name: Sprint-to-Stick Deceleration
explosive.job: Isolate a known forward braking boundary so the live task is not limited by an absent stopping strategy.
explosive.execution: Begin at 2 m; accelerate to 5 m and brake by 8 m using several controlled contacts. No sudden locked-leg stop. Rest 45 s between reps and 60 s before E5. Reduce entry speed for overshoot.

explosive.name: Split-Stance Broad Jump to Parallel Landing
explosive.job: Express forward drive from an asymmetric starting base, then share acceptance across both feet.
explosive.execution: Pause in a comfortable staggered stance, jump forward and land with feet parallel; no stance-switch jumps. Two starts each lead. Rest 30 s between attempts, 60 s before E6; reduce distance for rotation.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — forward
explosive.job: Link hip/knee extension to a forward release while keeping the athlete grounded; supports whole-body forward projection.
explosive.execution: Light ball, quarter squat, quick leg drive and low two-hand underhand release. No jump or return catch. Stay inside the marked throw zone. Rest 30 s between throws and 90 s before strength; reduce ball load for slow arm-dominated release.

stabilization.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — light
stabilization.job: Light ankle control against outward rolling during the first planted acceleration step.
stabilization.execution: With heel supported and shin still, turn the forefoot slightly outward against a light band held securely by the coach, away from the face. Return slowly; no ankle rolling or knee turn. Reduce tension/range for loss of control. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

stabilization.name: Heel-Dig Bridge Hold — light bilateral
stabilization.job: Easy posterior-chain positional tension before the stronger hinge; do not turn it into hamstring fatigue.
stabilization.execution: On a comfortable floor surface, heels down and knees bent; lift hips only to a stacked trunk and gently pull heels toward the hips without moving them. Keep easy and breathe; lower height for cramp or back extension. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

primary.name: Goblet Squat
primary.job: Bilateral knee/hip extension for projecting forward from the initial athletic stance.
primary.execution: Hold one dumbbell at the chest; sit between the hips with whole-foot pressure and rise smoothly. Use an owned depth; reduce load/range for heel lift or trunk collapse. 120 s between rounds and 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Reverse Lunge — dumbbells
primary.job: Front-leg force through the return step without another full two-set unilateral block.
primary.execution: Step one foot backward, lower under control, then use the front leg to return to standing. Keep the front heel down; shorten the step/load for wobble or push-off from the rear toes. Rest 90 s between sides; 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
primary.job: Retained hip-hinge anchor for braking with the hips back and returning to extension.
primary.execution: Hinge from standing with soft knees; keep weights close and stop descent where the pelvis/spine remain controlled. Finish tall without leaning back. Reduce range/load for rounding. 120 s between rounds and 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Partner Manual-Resistance Hamstring Curl
primary.job: Direct knee-flexor force supports control of the lower leg through the first running steps.
primary.execution: Lie prone on a comfortable floor surface; coach applies smooth resistance above the heel while the athlete bends and straightens the knee through an owned range. Keep hips down; no sudden pushes. Match resistance to 2–3 RIR, not a contest. If prone support/contact is unsuitable, use Seated Band Hamstring Curl instead, same sets/reps per side: sit on a stable bench, secure a light band at the heel with a coach holding steady forward tension, then pull the heel beneath the bench without moving the thigh. Qualify band/bench fit; no sudden release. This replaces only this slot and preserves totals. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise — supported standing, dumbbell
primary.job: Retained straighter-knee ankle push as the pursuit stride opens.
primary.execution: Stand on flat floor with a nearly straight knee and light hand support; raise the heel, pause briefly and lower for 2 seconds. No bounce or ankle roll. Reduce load when heel height declines. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, bent-knee
primary.job: Bent-knee ankle drive for the initial low stance; one set limits accumulated calf work.
primary.execution: Use a stable bench, knees near right angles, secure dumbbells on distal thighs above knees. Lower heels for 2 seconds to the floor, pause, then rise. Reduce load for bouncing or shortened range. Rest 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

post_sequence_audit.geometry_review: straight/parallel route with stated stopping buffers
